description: A comprehensive study of software systems used to efficiently store, manage, and retrieve data in Computer Science and Information Technology, encompassing relational databases, SQL, normalization, and transaction management.

sections.title: ER Model and Relational Model
sections.description: Conceptual and logical design methodologies utilized to systematically map complex real-world scenarios into highly structured database schemas.

key_concepts.explanation: An Entity is any real-world object or concept represented in the database (e.g., Student, Employee). Attributes are the distinct properties or characteristics that describe the entity (e.g., Name, Roll Number).

A Primary Key (PK) uniquely identifies every record in a table and strictly cannot contain null values. A Foreign Key (FK) establishes a definitive relationship between two tables and ensures referential integrity.

sections.title: Relational Algebra and SQL
sections.description: The foundational theoretical procedural language (Relational Algebra) and the universally adopted practical declarative language (SQL) used to query and manipulate relational data.

equations: Selection (sigma): Filters and selects rows (tuples) that satisfy a specific condition.
Projection (pi): Selects only specified columns (attributes) and automatically eliminates duplicates.
Cartesian Product (cross): Combines information from two relations by generating all possible combinations of their tuples.

results: Inner Join: Returns only the records that have matching values in both interconnected tables.
Left Outer Join: Returns all records from the left table, and the matched records from the right table (returns NULL for unmatched rows).
Full Outer Join: Returns all records when there is a match in either the left or right table, filling unmatched sides with NULL values.

sections.title: Database Normalization
sections.description: The systematic, step-by-step process of decomposing and organizing tables to severely minimize data redundancy and completely eliminate insertion, update, and deletion anomalies.

results: First Normal Form (1NF): Every attribute in the table must contain only atomic (indivisible) values. Multi-valued attributes are strictly prohibited.
Second Normal Form (2NF): The table must be in 1NF, and there must be absolutely no partial dependencies (i.e., non-prime attributes must depend on the entire primary key, not just a part of it).
Third Normal Form (3NF): The table must be in 2NF, and there must be zero transitive dependencies (non-prime attributes must not depend on other non-prime attributes).
Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF): A stricter, advanced version of 3NF where every determinant in the table must be a candidate key.

sections.title: Transactions and Concurrency Control
sections.description: Mechanisms to ensure that multiple concurrent database operations execute safely and leave the database in a consistent state, resilient to system crashes.

key_concepts.explanation: Atomicity (transaction executes completely or not at all), Consistency (database transitions from one valid state to another), Isolation (concurrent transactions do not interfere), and Durability (committed changes survive system failures).

The highest level of isolation. A theoretical concept ensuring that the concurrent execution of interleaved transactions yields the exact same final database state as if they were executed serially (one immediately after another).

results: Dirty Read: Occurs when a transaction is permitted to read uncommitted data modified by another transaction that might eventually roll back.
Unrepeatable Read: Occurs when a transaction reads the exact same row twice and gets entirely different values because another transaction successfully updated it in between the reads.
Phantom Read: Occurs when a transaction re-executes a query returning a set of rows, and finds that another transaction has inserted or deleted rows that satisfy the condition.

sections.title: Indexing and File Organization
sections.description: Advanced physical design techniques determining how data records are stored on magnetic disks and the utilization of indexing structures for rapid data retrieval.

key_concepts.explanation: The most universally implemented balanced tree data structure for database indexing. All actual data pointers reside exclusively at the leaf nodes, which are linked together as a linked list, facilitating incredibly fast sequential and range queries.

A highly efficient technique utilizing a mathematical hash function to map a search key directly to a specific data block address (bucket). It provides an exceptional O(1) retrieval time for exact-match queries but performs poorly on range queries.
